hero.title: Restoration Diagnostic
hero.description1: A structured method for identifying which key success factors for ecosystem restoration you already have in place, partially in place, or are missing within a country or landscape that has restoration opportunities.
hero.description2: A structured method for assessing ecosystem restoration readiness. The diagnostic will help you identify key success factors that you have in place, partially in place, or still need to consider how to include.

intro.heading: Prepare for the diagnostic
intro.description1: In this phase, you will have the opportunity to set the scope, choose stakeholder engagement methods, gather the necessary documentation, define the target geography or scale, and outline your restoration goals and timeline.
intro.description2: Taking time to prepare ensures the diagnostic is focused, well-supported, and aligned with your restoration context.
intro.description3: There are 2 parts to this step:

scope.title: Set the scope
scope.description: Define the target landscape, time horizon, and restoration goals.

approach.title: Plan your diagnostic approach
approach.description: Decide how you will engage stakeholders and gather supporting materials.

step1.heading: Target geography
step1.description: The target geography defines the area or scale where the diagnostic will be applied. This may be a country, sub-national administrative area, municipality, watershed, biome, or ecological region.

restorationBoundary.label: Restoration boundary link
restorationBoundary.caption: Add a link to a GIS dataset or boundary file

ecosystems.label: Capture ecosystem types
ecosystems.description: Select all ecosystem types present in your target area

step2.heading: Time horizon
step2.description: The time horizon should reflect the long-term nature of restoration, even if actions begin in the short term. It may align with an existing national or sub-national planning cycle or strategy.

step3.heading: Restoration goals
step3.description: Describe your overarching goals for restoration. Consider objectives related to biodiversity, climate mitigation, livelihoods, and ecosystem services.
step3.description1: Restoration goals describe the intended outcomes for the landscape. These may focus on a single ecosystem type or on a mix of ecosystems.
step3.description2: Goals commonly relate to biodiversity conservation, climate mitigation or adaptation, livelihood improvement, water security, or food production.
step3.description3: Restoration goals can be described either before or after running the diagnostic, depending on the context and how the diagnostic is completed.

step4.heading: Define engagement strategy
step4.description: You will engage stakeholders at different stages of the diagnostic. Review the suggested approaches below and plan how you will involve them. You may wish to outline your strategy below.

participatory.title: Participatory workshops
participatory.content:
• Convene a half-day or full-day workshop (virtual or in-person)
  • Use structured facilitation to guide responses
  • Best when time is limited and participation is desired
items: Bring together diverse stakeholders to discuss and answer questions collaboratively
Facilitates dialogue and ensures multiple perspectives are considered
Best for building consensus and shared understanding

interviews.title: Interviews / focus groups
interviews.content:
• Semi-structured interviews with key actors
  • Useful for sensitive topics (e.g., tenure insecurity, governance challenges)
items: Conduct one-on-one or small group discussions with key informants
Allows for in-depth exploration of specific topics
Useful when certain stakeholders cannot attend larger workshops

distributed.title: Distributed completion
distributed.content:
• Share the worksheet found under Step 2 with stakeholders
  • Ask them to complete sections relevant to their expertise
  • Coordinate synthesis and discussion afterward
items: Share the diagnostic with stakeholders to complete independently
Allows individuals to respond at their own pace
May require consolidation of multiple responses

notes.label: Engagement strategy notes
notes.placeholder: Add any notes about your engagement approach...

step5.heading: Gather supporting materials
step5.description: Before starting the diagnostic, it is useful to gather key documents and data sources in order to refer to them as evidence. We recommend organising them in a shared folder so all contributors can access the same evidence during the diagnostic.

policy.title: Policy & legal context
policy.content:
• National restoration strategies or programs.
  • Laws and regulations (Forestry, Agriculture, Land Use, Water).
  • International commitments (UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD).
  • National development plans.
items: National or regional restoration commitments and policies
Land tenure regulations and customary rights frameworks
Environmental protection laws and enforcement mechanisms

implementation.title: Implementation & planning
implementation.content:
• Sub-national or regional restoration action plans.
  • Municipal development plans for the target landscapes.
  • Donor-funded program documentation.
  • Existing institutional budgets and organizational charts.
items: Existing restoration plans or strategies
Budget allocations and funding sources
Stakeholder mapping and engagement records

biophysical.title: Biophysical & socioeconomic data
biophysical.content:
• Land cover and land degradation assessments.
  • Restoration opportunity maps (e.g., ROAM outputs).
  • Socioeconomic data (tenure status, livelihood dependence, market analyses).
items: Land use and land cover maps
Biodiversity assessments and species inventories
Socioeconomic profiles of local communities

monitoring.title: Monitoring & baselines
monitoring.content:
• Data from landscape monitoring systems (e.g., Global Forest Watch).
  • Existing restoration indicators and historical progress reports.
items: Baseline data on ecosystem condition
Historical trends in land degradation or restoration
Existing monitoring frameworks or indicators

sharedFolder.label: Shared folder link
sharedFolder.placeholder: Enter URL to shared folder (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox)
sharedFolder.caption: This link will be shown to anyone you provide access to the Diagnostic. Ensure everyone supporting the diagnostic has permission to view.

whySetTargetGeography.title: Why set the target geography
whySetTargetGeography.content: Defining the geographic scope helps ensure that your diagnostic responses are contextually relevant and that recommendations can be tailored to your specific landscape or jurisdiction. It also helps identify which stakeholders should be engaged and what data sources are most applicable.

howToDoIt.title: How to do it
howToDoIt.content: Start by identifying the administrative or ecological boundary of your restoration area. Consider whether your focus is national policy, a subnational jurisdiction, a specific landscape, or an individual site. Select all ecosystem types present in your target area to help guide your responses to ecosystem-specific questions.

whySetTimeHorizon.title: Why set the time horizon
whySetTimeHorizon.content: Establishing a time horizon helps set realistic expectations for restoration outcomes and aligns your diagnostic responses with achievable milestones. Different restoration activities yield results over different timescales, from immediate interventions to long-term ecological recovery.

howToDoIt.title: How to do it
howToDoIt.content: Consider the expected duration of your restoration activities, from initial planning through implementation and monitoring. Typical restoration periods range from 5 to 30 years, depending on ecosystem type and restoration goals. If you're unsure, you can leave this field blank or provide an estimate.

whySetRestorationGoals.title: Why set restoration goals
whySetRestorationGoals.content: Clearly articulated restoration goals provide direction for your diagnostic and help ensure that your responses align with your intended outcomes. Goals may focus on biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, livelihood improvement, water security, or other ecosystem services.

howToDoIt.title: How to do it
howToDoIt.content: Describe what you hope to achieve through restoration in your target area. Be as specific as possible about environmental, social, and economic objectives. Consider both ecological outcomes (e.g., forest cover, species recovery) and socioeconomic benefits (e.g., improved livelihoods, enhanced resilience).

designingEngagement.title: Designing stakeholder engagement
designingEngagement.content: Effective stakeholder engagement ensures that diverse perspectives are included in the diagnostic. Consider who should be involved, including government agencies, local communities, Indigenous Peoples, civil society organizations, and private sector actors.

ensuringInclusion.title: Ensuring inclusion and equity
ensuringInclusion.content:
Some participants may hesitate to share in group settings, and local social/gender dynamics can exclude some groups. The coordinating team should adapt engagement methods to ensure diverse perspectives are captured. This can be done by:

  • Holding separate focus groups for women and/or Indigenous communities
  • Using local languages
  • Including trusted intermediaries
  • Providing travel/compensation where needed
  • Creating safe space agreements
  • Allowing anonymous written input for sensitive questions
items: Actively seek out voices from marginalized or underrepresented groups, including women, youth, and Indigenous Peoples
Consider language, accessibility, and timing when planning engagement activities
Provide sufficient context and preparation materials so all participants can contribute meaningfully
Document who participated and how their input was incorporated

preparingEvidence.title: Preparing your evidence
preparingEvidence.content:
The diagnostic asks you to assess whether key enabling conditions are in place. To answer confidently and consistently, you will need to refer to existing documents, data sources, and policy materials.

Please note that evidence can be collected throughout the entire process, if necessary.

organizingAccess.title: Organizing access to documents
organizingAccess.content: Add links to a shared folder or individual documents stored online (for example, in a shared drive or document platform). This ensures that everyone involved can quickly access the same information during workshops or distributed completion.
